sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is the difference between a generalised package and a customised package?
questions.answer: A generalised package is ready-made, user-friendly software for common needs that anyone can buy, e.g. word processors, spreadsheets, DBMS. A customised package is developed to meet the specific needs of one organisation, e.g. a student management system or payroll for a company.

or.q: Define the memory system of a computer and give one example of each type of memory.
or.answer: The memory system stores data and instructions. Primary (main) memory is accessed directly by the CPU, e.g. RAM (and ROM). Secondary memory stores data permanently, e.g. hard disk, CD/DVD, pen drive.

questions.q: What is computer organisation?
questions.answer: Computer organisation is the way the parts of a computer are arranged to work together. A computer has an input unit, a memory unit, a control unit, an arithmetic logic unit and an output unit; it accepts input, stores and processes it under the control unit and gives output.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: What are compilers? Why are they needed? What are the programs before and after translation called?
questions.answer: A compiler is software that reads a program written in a high-level language and translates it into an equivalent program in machine language. It is needed because the computer understands only machine language (0s and 1s). The program written by the programmer is the source program; the program produced after translation is the object program.

questions.q: Write the steps to edit existing data records in mail merge.
questions.answer: (1) In step 3 of the wizard choose 'Use an existing list' and click Browse. (2) Select the data file and click Open. (3) Click Edit Recipient List. (4) Move to the record using the arrow buttons, record number or Find. (5) Change the entries and save the changes.

questions.q: Name three ways of creating a data source in mail merge.
questions.answer: (1) Type a new list in the Mail Merge Wizard (New Address List). (2) Use a table in a Word document. (3) Use an Excel worksheet (or an Access database / RTF file).

questions.q: Expand (any three): ISP, PC, ISDN, TCP, TLD.
questions.answer: ISP — Internet Service Provider; PC — Personal Computer; ISDN — Integrated Services Digital Network; TCP — Transmission Control Protocol; TLD — Top-Level Domain.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: (a) Explain Telnet and FTP. (b) Explain organisational domains and geographical domains.
questions.answer:
(a) Telnet is a network protocol used on the Internet or a LAN; the Telnet program connects your PC to a server so that commands you type run on the server, letting you control it remotely. FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is used to exchange files over a TCP/IP network: an FTP client connects to an FTP server to upload, download, rename or delete files.
(b) Organisational domains show the type of organisation: .ac, .com, .edu, .gov, .net, .org. Geographical domains are two-letter country codes: .in (India), .uk, .us, .au, .jp.

or.q: What happens to a piece of data when it is transferred over the Internet? Explain.
or.answer: It is broken into equal-sized packets; a header saying where each packet came from, where it is going and how it fits with the others is added; each packet travels from computer to computer, each deciding the next hop, so packets may follow different routes; at the destination they are checked and reassembled in order.
